takeaway: A Lanz incision is a transverse incision across McBurney's point, lateral to rectus abdominis, so rectus is not divided. Divided: skin, superficial fascia, external and internal oblique, transversus, peritoneum.

lines.text: A ten-year-old boy has an open appendicectomy through a Lanz incision.
It is a transverse incision across McBurney's point, a third of the way from the anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus.
You cut through skin, then superficial fascia, including Scarpa's fascia,
then the muscles: external oblique, internal oblique and transversus abdominis, and finally the peritoneum.
But rectus abdominis lies in the centre of the abdomen.
The Lanz incision is lateral to it, so rectus abdominis is the one not divided.
And as a bonus, the Lanz incision is cosmetically better.
